title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Issuing the Guiding Opinions on Further Improving the Adjudication of Civil Cases Involving Agriculture under the Current Circumstances
keywords_en: Property Rights; Further Improving Civil Cases Involving Agriculture
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Issuing the "Guiding Opinions on Further Improving the Trial of Civil Cases Involving Agriculture under the Current Situation"

Fa Fa [2009] No. 37

The Higher People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government, the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army, and the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the Higher People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region:

The Guiding Opinions on Further Improving the Trial of Civil Cases Involving Agriculture under the Current Situation of the Supreme People's Court are hereby issued to you. Please implement them earnestly in light of local realities.

June 19, 2009

Guiding Opinions on Further Improving the Trial of Civil Cases Involving Agriculture under the Current Situation

At present, affected by the continuous spread and expansion of the international financial crisis, the number of civil cases involving agriculture has increased substantially, and many new situations and new problems have emerged in these cases. Giving full play to the function of adjudication, doing a good job in the trial of civil cases involving agriculture, and actively responding to the challenges brought by the international financial crisis will be an important part of the civil trial work of the people's courts for a period to come, especially this year. People's courts at all levels must earnestly adhere to the socialist rule of law concept, firmly establish the awareness of serving the overall situation and administering justice for the people, and deeply understand the significance of carrying out the trial of civil cases involving agriculture under the current situation, especially under the influence of the international financial crisis. In order to effectively handle the trial of civil cases involving agriculture under the current situation, the following opinions are hereby proposed in accordance with relevant laws and national policies:

1. Strictly implement the provisions of the Property Law, the Rural Land Contract Law, and the judicial interpretation of the Supreme People's Court, such as the Interpretation on Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Disputes over Rural Land Contracting, and increase the intensity of trial of disputes such as illegal recovery or adjustment of contracted land that infringe upon the right to land contractual management, especially disputes involving the rights and interests of migrant workers in land contractual management, and effectively safeguard all rights and interests of farmers in land contractual management.

2. Coordinate and balance the relationship between maintaining the right to land contractual management and promoting the transfer of the right to land contractual management. An important goal of promoting the transfer of the right to land contractual management is to increase farmers' income and enhance the level and competitiveness of agricultural development. In accordance with the principle of being conducive to both the orderly and standardized transfer of the right to land contractual management and the full protection of farmers' various lawful rights and interests in land contracting, cases involving disputes that violate laws and national policies and harm farmers' right to land contractual management under the guise of transferring the right to land contractual management shall be tried properly.

3. For disputes arising from the obviously low transfer fees for the right to land contractual management of returning migrant workers or the expiration of the transfer contract term not yet due after their return, especially cases where returning migrant workers thus fall into living difficulties, efforts should be made to strengthen mediation under the leadership of the local party committee and with the support of the government, and more work should be done on the opposing party to strive for a balance of interests between the two parties. If mediation fails, the case shall be handled properly according to the principle of fairness based on the specific circumstances of the parties and the case, so as to avoid, to the greatest extent possible, new social problems caused by the lack of livelihood of returning migrant workers.

4. Earnestly try cases of tort disputes and contract disputes such as product quality and damages arising during the implementation of national policies to boost domestic demand, such as home appliances to the countryside, automobiles to the countryside, agricultural machinery to the countryside, and trade-in of home appliances and automobiles, and fully protect the legitimate rights and interests of farmers in accordance with the law, providing judicial guarantees for relevant national preferential policies to genuinely benefit the masses of farmers.

5. Further leverage the function of judicial adjudication to guide and establish a social concept of equality between urban and rural areas in all aspects, including labor conditions, production safety, labor remuneration, and work-related injury, medical, and pension insurance. For disputes arising from employment discrimination and other such matters, trial and related work shall be carried out in accordance with the guiding principles of promoting equal urban-rural employment, advancing the integration of urban-rural economic and social development, and effectively alleviating rural employment pressure.

6. Continuously strengthen the judicial protection of the legitimate rights and interests of migrant workers who have returned to start businesses or work locally, actively explore and steadily advance judicial protection system measures for the legitimate rights and interests of migrant workers returning to start businesses or work locally, and create a favorable judicial environment for migrant workers to return to start businesses or work locally.

7. In accordance with the relevant provisions of the Property Law and the judicial interpretation of the Supreme People's Court, such as the Interpretation on Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Disputes over Rural Land Contracting, properly handle disputes over the distribution of land acquisition compensation fees. When trying cases arising from differential treatment in the distribution plan of land compensation fees, which infringes upon the interests of the parties, the legitimate rights and interests of rural collective members, especially women, children, and migrant workers, shall be fully protected in accordance with the law.

8. Conscientiously implement the Measures for the Payment of Litigation Costs, continue to increase judicial assistance for impoverished rural people, and strengthen litigation tips and guidance. For farmer litigants who are genuinely in financial difficulty, especially those in special difficult circumstances, measures to defer, reduce, or exempt litigation costs shall be actively taken to ensure that farmer litigants who meet the conditions for assistance can afford to file a lawsuit.

9. Promptly establish and improve the mechanisms for the diversion of simple and complex cases and expedited adjudication, quickly resolve conflicts, and improve litigation efficiency. For remote areas or areas with concentrated disputes, the people's tribunals shall increase the intensity of circuit trials, strive to achieve on-site case filing, on-site trial, immediate mediation, immediate conclusion, and on-site enforcement, and effectively facilitate the litigation of the farmer masses.

10. In light of the current situation, earnestly carry out the work of handling petition letters and visits related to rural litigation, and strive to fundamentally prevent and reduce the occurrence of such cases. Strengthen source management, implement the system of separating litigation from petitions, and improve the working mechanism for receiving, diverting, and handling petition cases. Explore the establishment of a mechanism for the finalization of petition cases under the leadership of the party committee, and work with relevant departments to gradually improve the fund system for assisting petitioners who meet the conditions for assistance.

11. Actively explore and steadily advance the diversified dispute resolution mechanism in rural areas, guide parties to use methods such as rural land contract arbitration and mediation to resolve disputes, effectively reduce the levels and links of dispute resolution, and lower the cost of conflict resolution. Focus on linkage and collaboration with grassroots governments, villagers' self-governing organizations, and other diversified dispute resolution entities, build a full-coverage network for dispute resolution, and strive to resolve conflicts before litigation and eliminate them in their infancy.

12. Under the leadership of the local party committee, strengthen communication and contact with the government and relevant departments, support the government's dominant role in resolving major risks, and focus on promoting the establishment of a multi-level, all-round collaborative linkage resolution mechanism to form a joint force and avoid risk spread and loss of control. Establish a smooth early warning mechanism to promptly discover major litigation-related information; improve the guidance mechanism to strengthen trial guidance for major cases; improve emergency plans to properly handle sensitive and group disputes. New situations and new problems arising in the trial of civil cases involving agriculture under the influence of the international financial crisis shall be promptly and seriously studied, countermeasures shall be proposed as soon as possible, and if necessary, reported to our court in a timely manner level by level.
